change: The layout oracle is Chrome-only. run_oracle.py's three-way (C# reference vs core, Chrome arbitrating) is retired from check.sh and CI; chrome_sweep.py --chrome-metrics --max-worst 1.5 --known-gaps is the gate. The corpus and its Chrome captures are tracked.
mode: weva_dump --chrome-metrics: the browser-semantics walk (full transform applied to every corner, inline fragments unioned, as getBoundingClientRect does). The default walk keeps the C# reference's box semantics and is not what a Chrome comparison should use.

captures.note: captured with every fixture asset beside the page; a capture taken without them records Chrome's broken-image placeholder and is wrong, which is how cov-image first read 176px off

ceiling_rationale: hand 52/52 agree; harvest's five differing cases are inside 1.0px; samples' text-baseline rounding tops out at 1.3px at 1280 wide; the first genuine divergence in any corpus is 356px (a known gap)

harvest.source: Tools/oracle/harvest_corpus.py over Packages/com.wevaui/Tests (37 files); replaces the earlier 210-case snapshot

samples.note: both exceed the ceiling identically against the pre-existing captures; the three-way masked them because the C# reference agreed with the core

correction: The first version of this receipt, and of known-gaps/chrome-sweep.txt, ran the dump in its default walk and recorded 12 excused samples, nine of them classified as capture-tool artefacts (transformed AABB, inline union, image loading). They were the dump mode, not tool limits: in --chrome-metrics mode all nine agree. Recorded so the mistake is not repeated.
also_found: check.sh tested $GCC/tools/weva_dump (lowercase) since the flatten; the build tree is Tools/, so the layout oracle and six other steps had been skipping silently. Re-cased; a gate that cannot run now fails.
verified_by: the check.sh chrome_oracle function run verbatim against the tracked corpus (scratchpad/oracle-step.sh): failures=0
